paper.title_en: A Quantitative Method to Investigate the Spectral Class Time Evolution of Novae
paper.abstract_en: Novae are spectroscopically classified as Fe II or He/N according to the dominance of Fe II, or He and N emission lines in their pre-nebular spectra, while spectra exhibiting both are classified as hybrid. Whereas the spectral class of a nova is known to correlate with its progenitor properties, a recent detailed spectroscopic follow-up of ten novae suggests instead a time evolution from "early He/N" to "Fe II" and to "late He/N". We investigate here this apparent contradiction using a spectroscopic dataset of 26 novae from the Astronomical Ring for Amateur Spectroscopy (ARAS) Database. For this purpose we introduce a quantitative coefficient, $κ$, defined as the ratio of the flux of the Fe II $λ$5169 line to the mean flux of five He and N emission lines, with $κ> 1$ indicating Fe II-dominated spectra and $κ< 1$ indicating He/N-dominated spectra. This coefficient is shown to provide a reliable quantitative tool for tracing nova spectral evolution while reducing biases from incomplete coverage. A significant fraction of the novae in our sample exhibit at least one transition between Fe II- and He/N-dominated phases. The time evolution of $κ$ closely follows their optical light-curves, repeatedly crossing unity in novae exhibiting jitters, which reveal non-monotonic spectral evolution. Since the light-curve shapes and their time-scales depend on intrinsic progenitor properties, particularly white dwarf mass, they also determine the duration of Fe II- and He/N-dominated phases, introducing a bias in spectral classification when it relies on early, sparse spectra.
